citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not identify three budgies with a health concern prior to today’s inspection. One approximately 2-week-old
budgie chick was observed walking around its cage outside its nest box. It had semi dried blood over its head that
extended near its face. Present in another cage was an adult female budgie who had feather loss at the base of her tail.
Upon further observation it was noted that she had a red tubular tissue protruding underneath the tail near its cloaca. The
third bird, an adult male budgie, was observed with a circular patch of feather loss around its right eye. The edges of
feathers around this area were yellow tinged in color and semi-wet in appearance giving the appearance of crusting. The
right eye was clear, skin was pink to mottled red, and had a drying red scab above its cheek. When the licensee was
asked about these birds and if he had noticed these issues he stated he had not noted them prior to today’s inspection.
Inadequate daily observations can result in failure to identify medical issues and as a result delay treatment. Daily
observation must be performed on all animals to assess their health and well-being and provide treatment as needed.
Direct and frequent communication with the attending veterinarian is required so that timely and accurate information on
problems of animal health can be conveyed to the attending veterinarian.
Correct from this day 7/29/26, on forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
